content:
Hollywood is increasingly viewing YouTube as a major competitor, and according to a new report, free versions of streaming platforms like Disney+ and Paramount+ may be the way to counter it.

Streaming platforms like Disney+, Paramount+, and Netflix are exploring free versions in different ways

Recently, Disney's Chief Product and Technology Officer Adam Smith was reportedly "talking about launching free-tier content at a streaming town hall meeting."

The plan aims to remove the barriers posed by the Disney+ paywall in order to expand reach. When viewers are already regularly using the app, Disney can more easily upsell them to paid subscriptions.

Paramount reportedly has a similar idea: "According to an internal presentation obtained by Business Insider, Paramount's flagship streaming platform plans to expand the content of movies and shows that can be watched without a subscription."

Netflix's comments on free service are primarily aimed at markets outside the United States. But depending on how free versions of other streaming platforms perform, this situation could change at any time.

Each streaming platform appears to be partly driven by YouTube's growing user engagement and market share. Disney+ had previously planned to add YouTube-like, user-generated free content. But with the dissolution of Sora and the collapse of Disney's partnership with OpenAI, the future of such plans has become uncertain.

What do you think about streaming platforms launching more free streaming tiers? Let us know in the comments.
